subject: platform/devstats
professional: a senior release/DevOps engineer who reports DORA-style delivery metrics to engineering leadership; first questions: do the counts match the system of record, are percentiles computed correctly, are proxies labelled as proxies, and does missing data read as missing rather than zero?

evidence.correctness: Ran fromGit/fromRuns/fromAllocation/quantile against the checkout (now=2026-11-08T12:00Z) and recomputed with other tools. (1) merges_per_day: node gave 24 on 11-07 and 26 on 11-08 (50 total); `git log --first-parent --format=%ct | awk strftime | uniq -c` gave the same 24/26. (2) fromRuns by_track over the 30-day window: node ventures 1854 runs, success 0.87, ci_failures_mean 5.4, 430 measured, median $0.66; research 1767/0.94/0.05/818/0.84; process 531/0.76/2.86/183/0.47; an independent Python json+statistics script gave identical figures for all three tracks and 5563 records total. (3) allocation periods: node today/7d/all = 16/1118/5280 runs; Python filter (no `source`, date<=today) gave 16/1118/5280. (4) quantile([1,2,3,4,10],0.9)=7.6, matching numpy's linear-interpolation default by formula; single value and empty list behave (5, null). (5) delivery() on a hand-built fixture (validate runs fail@1h,2h, pass@5h, fail@7h, pass@8h, fail@10h; now=12h; merge@3h, deploy created 4h done 4.5h): by hand restore spells [4h,1h] -> p50 2.5, p90 3.7, open spell 2h -> red_hours 7, 3 red spells, merge-to-live 90 min; tool output matched exactly. Not checked: the GitHub-API paths against the live API (only mocked fetch), and the live site (marisstella.app unreachable through the proxy, HTTP 000).
evidence.completeness: README lists 8 sections. Checked end to end locally: git merges/lead time/reverts (works, but see lead time defect), run records, allocation incl. next-lane forecast, rendering (test + build path). GitHub PR/review, CI per-day counts, and delivery sections run only against mocked fetch in tests plus my hand fixtures; without a token they correctly return available:false with a reason. build.mjs and render.mjs read; no TODOs or stubs found. Branch-to-merge time is listed as a git-log source but in this repository's squash-merge history it can never be measured (0 merge commits among 50 first-parent commits; lead_time n=0), so one advertised row is permanently 'not measured' (honestly labelled).
evidence.verification: `node --test platform/devstats/*.test.mjs`: 24 pass, 0 fail, 1.5 s. Hand-seeded mutations in core logic (each reverted, git diff of platform/ empty afterwards): (a) countRunsByDay reuse guard `prevAt >= start + 2*DAY` -> `prevAt >= start`: caught (1 fail); (b) countSlice cap `n < COUNT_CAP` -> `<=`: caught (2 fail); (c) delivery merge-to-live `x.created >= at` -> `>= at - 1h`: caught (1 fail); (d) quantile floors the interpolation position: caught (2 fail); (e) delivery red-spell start `redSince ??= t` -> `redSince = t` (restarts a spell on each consecutive failure, understating time to restore and red hours): NOT caught, 24 pass. The test fixtures have no consecutive failures on a gate. Also dropping 'unbreak' from the fix-forward regex went unnoticed. Core arithmetic is well covered, state-machine edge cases less so.
evidence.craft: Read devstats.mjs (599 lines), allocation.mjs (303), build.mjs, render.mjs (top and key lines), tests. Strengths: pure functions separated from I/O, injected fetch and clock, escaping in render, errors surfaced as {available:false, reason}, cap-halving counter. Defects: reverts regex `^Revert\b|\brevert(s|ed)?\b.*#\d+` matches any squash subject that merely contains the word revert plus a PR number (e.g. 'process: add revert detection to the dashboard (#13001)' -> true) and fix-forward regex matches 'fix the main page layout (#1)'; both are heuristics presented as counts. `ghJson` and `ghPages` duplicate auth headers; `tally` is defined in both devstats.mjs and allocation.mjs with different meaning; fromGitHub is a ~90-line function; fromGit's ventures_added uses `ventures/*/VENTURE.yaml` pathspec on a shallow clone, where the root commit makes every file 'added' (1335 here, equal to the full inventory) - production uses fetch-depth 3000 so it is right there but nothing guards it. Silent catch blocks in fromGit lead-time and added() return null/skip without a note.
evidence.claims: Checked: README 'CI runs ... exact, halved at the 2,500 cap' -> countSlice + 2 tests, true; 'newest 1,000 completed runs' -> SAMPLE_PAGES=10 x 100, true; 'metric with no source shown as not measured, never zero' -> render.mjs show(), test 'marks missing data', true; 'a count that hit an API cap is labelled a floor' -> coverage.note, true; 'previous stats.json avoids recounting' -> reuse test, true; allocation attribution order record > merge subject > mention -> attribute() + test, true; render has no off-origin requests -> test asserts it. Weaker: README table says lead time is from 'git log' as branch-to-merge time without saying it is empty under squash merges (the in-page note does say so); the code comment calls the delivery block 'the four DORA metrics' though it computes merge-to-live, failed share of gate runs and gate restore time, not deploy-caused change-failure rate. No product disclaimer needed (internal telemetry). Live page not loaded (proxy).
evidence.fitness: Job: an operator wants to know whether main is healthy, how fast merges reach production, where agent runs go. Walked through: build.mjs without a token produces a page with git/run/allocation data and explicit 'not measured' for API sections; with a token the code path is covered by mocks. Run counts, per-track cost and allocation matched independent recomputation, red spells and merge-to-live matched hand arithmetic, so a reader can act on them. Limits: lead time is dead under squash merges, so the GitHub PR cycle time is the only usable proxy; CI sampling reflects only the newest 1,000 runs (stated).
evidence.domain: Compared against DORA (Accelerate / State of DevOps) definitions. Lead time for changes should be first commit to production; here merge-to-live (merge to end of first passing deploy run created after it) is used, which excludes review time, though PR cycle hours supplement it. Deployment frequency = passing portfolio-pages runs on main: reasonable. Change failure rate should be the share of deploys causing a degradation; here it is the failed share of gate runs (a CI-failure rate), a different quantity. MTTR is approximated by gate red-spell restore time. Medians/p90 with linear interpolation and p50/p90 rather than means are correct practice, spells beginning before the window are noted, caps are floors. A DORA practitioner would accept it as a CI-health and throughput dashboard but would not call the failure and recovery numbers DORA's.

defects.what: Revert and fix-forward counts are keyword heuristics with false positives: any squash subject containing 'revert' and a PR number counts as a revert; 'fix the main page ...' counts as a fix-forward of a red main. Counts shown on the page as facts.

Branch-to-merge time (README row, dashboard tile) can never be measured in a squash-merge repository: it only reads true merge commits, so n=0 and the tile is permanently 'not measured'. README does not say so.

Hand-seeded mutation `redSince ??= t` -> `redSince = t` in delivery() survives all 24 tests: no test has consecutive failures in a gate, so time-to-restore and red hours could be silently understated.
delivery block described as 'the four DORA metrics' but change-failure rate is a CI gate-run failure share, not deploys causing incidents; lead time excludes pre-merge time.
ventures_added uses a pathspec over git log that counts every file as added when the clone is shallow (1335 here); correct only with the production fetch-depth of 3000, unguarded.
GitHub API sections (PRs, reviews, CI counts, delivery) are verified only by mocked fetch; no live check was possible and the tests do not contract-test the API shapes.
Duplicated helpers: ghJson and ghPages repeat headers; two different `tally` functions in sibling modules.

verdict: A competent, honestly-labelled internal telemetry dashboard whose arithmetic I could reproduce: git merges per day, per-track run statistics and cost medians, allocation counts and quantile all matched independent Python/awk/numpy-formula recomputation, and the delivery red-spell and merge-to-live numbers matched hand calculation. 24 tests pass and four of five seeded mutations were caught, but the red-spell state machine mutation survived. Weaknesses are heuristic revert/fix-forward counts that false-positive on ordinary subjects, a lead-time metric that is structurally empty under squash merging, and delivery metrics that depart from DORA definitions while borrowing the name. It meets the bar (correctness, claims, verification all 3; median 3), without room to spare. Live site and live GitHub API were not reachable from this session.
